ai.description: *Hemidactylus sahgali* (Gekkonidae) reaches 50 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a white belly. Distinctive features include a strongly tuberculate dorsum and a tail with whorls.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus sahgali* is best distinguished by its unique, strongly keeled, trihedral tubercles that form distinct longitudinal rows along its back and tail.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus sahgali* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations on termite mounds and rock outcrops.
ai.behavior: Sahgal’s Termite Hill Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects while utilizing the crevices of termite mounds for shelter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus sahgali* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus sahgali* is endemic to the dry, rocky landscapes of the Aravalli Range in Rajasthan, India, typically found at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
